title: One unplaceable-reference rule replaces six reference lints
summary: This change collapses six separate reference lints (bare-reference, reference-without-label, reference-without-link, chat-local-reference, undefined-name, undefined-name-at-start) into a single `unplaceable-reference` rule backed by a new candidate engine in `crates/osf/src/lints/writing/reference.rs`. The engine finds numbers, phrases, times and names in a paragraph, then decides whether the paragraph itself places each one — a link, a bracketed or colon description, a repository named in the same sentence, a file path, a list item, an absolute date, a known name, or a definer sentence. Findings carry an `Evidence` value, and `resolve` now short-circuits statistical evidence to a warning that only advises, so a guess can never block a reply. The rule is wired into the writing lint pipeline, the skill and scan resolvers, and the stop hook, with 46 new fixtures and two new end-to-end test suites measuring precision and recall.

lanes.label: Entry points
lanes.subtitle: hooks, CLI, commit checks
lanes.summary: The surfaces that hand text to the linter: the stop hook, the prompt hook, the commit-message check and the scan command.

lanes.label: Lint core
lanes.subtitle: crates/osf-lint-core
lanes.summary: Shared rule machinery: the finding type, the evidence marker, and the level/remediation resolver that every caller now feeds evidence into.

lanes.label: Writing rules
lanes.subtitle: crates/osf/src/lints/writing
lanes.summary: The writing lint pipeline and the new candidate engine that decides whether a reference is placed by its own paragraph.

lanes.label: Fixtures and tests
lanes.subtitle: tests/fixtures/writing/unplaceable
lanes.summary: 46 labelled fixtures plus two end-to-end suites that pin the rule's behaviour at the hook, the commit check and the precision/recall table.

nodes.label: Stop hook
nodes.subtitle: crates/osf/src/hook.rs
nodes.summary: Reads the last assistant message from stdin and refuses the turn when a blocking finding is present. A reply whose only finding is a weak-evidence name is no longer refused.

nodes.label: Prompt hook
nodes.subtitle: hook prompt
nodes.summary: Prints the reminder shown on every prompt. It must never name a retired rule id, which the new end-to-end test asserts.

nodes.label: Commit-message check
nodes.subtitle: osf lint writing --context commit
nodes.summary: Lints a commit message file. The same relative time that a transcript may use fails here, because commit context is durable.

nodes.label: Scan command
nodes.subtitle: crates/osf/src/scan/mod.rs
nodes.summary: Resolves each scan finding's level and remediation, now passing the finding's own evidence through to the resolver.

nodes.label: resolve()
nodes.subtitle: osf_lint_core::resolve
nodes.summary: Maps class, group, context, exception and evidence to a level and remediation. Statistical evidence now returns Warning/Advise before any other rule is consulted, so a guess never blocks.

nodes.label: Evidence
nodes.subtitle: Deterministic | Statistical
nodes.summary: Marks whether a finding rests on a fact or a guess. Only the new rule sets Statistical today; every older rule is treated as deterministic.

nodes.label: Finding
nodes.subtitle: rule, excerpt, level, remediation, evidence
nodes.summary: The shared finding record. It now carries an evidence marker that the resolvers read.

nodes.label: lint_writing()
nodes.subtitle: crates/osf/src/lints/writing/mod.rs
nodes.summary: Runs the per-sentence, undefined-name and new unplaceable-reference passes, then applies context. Only the new rule's own evidence reaches the resolver; older rules stay deterministic until retired.

nodes.label: unplaceable_reference()
nodes.subtitle: crates/osf/src/lints/writing/rules.rs
nodes.summary: Walks each paragraph's candidates, keeps the first use of each name, picks one paragraph to report a repeated name from, and emits a finding for every candidate the paragraph does not place.

nodes.label: candidates()
nodes.subtitle: crates/osf/src/lints/writing/reference.rs
nodes.summary: Finds numbers, phrases, times and names in one paragraph, masks quoted and backticked spans, and keeps the longest candidate per kind when two overlap.

nodes.label: is_placed()
nodes.subtitle: number, phrase, time, name
nodes.summary: Decides whether the paragraph itself resolves a candidate: a link, a bracketed or colon description, a repository in the same sentence, a file path, a list item, an absolute date, a known name, or a definer sentence.

nodes.label: KnownNames
nodes.subtitle: built-in list plus project file
nodes.summary: The list of names a reader is assumed to know. Sonnet, Opus and Haiku were added, and a generic-word check lets a project name exclude a following number while a generic label word does not.

nodes.label: RULE_META
nodes.subtitle: crates/osf/src/lints/writing/meta.rs
nodes.summary: The doc text and class/group metadata for every writing rule. A new entry documents unplaceable-reference, and several examples were reworded to avoid tripping the new rule.

nodes.label: Unplaceable fixtures
nodes.subtitle: 46 labelled markdown files
nodes.summary: Each fixture carries an osf-unplaceable header naming its label, kind, target and reason, so the measure suite can score precision and recall per kind.

nodes.label: unplaceable_measure
nodes.subtitle: precision and recall table
nodes.summary: Runs the lint over every fixture, scores true and false positives per kind, and requires 100% precision and recall with no stray findings.

nodes.label: unplaceable_checkpoints
nodes.subtitle: end-to-end against the binary
nodes.summary: Drives the compiled osf binary at the stop hook, the commit-message check and the prompt hook, proving the rule fires and refuses where it should and never names a deleted rule id.

edges.label: last assistant message
edges.summary: The stop hook hands the reply to the writing lint, which now runs the unplaceable-reference pass over it.

edges.label: commit message, context commit
edges.summary: The commit-message check runs the same pipeline in commit context, where relative times are candidates.

edges.label: class, group, context, exception, evidence
edges.summary: The scan resolver now forwards the finding's evidence into resolve.

edges.label: doc, known names, config, context
edges.summary: The pipeline calls the new rule once per document, after the per-sentence and undefined-name passes.

edges.label: paragraph, config, known names, run counts
edges.summary: For each paragraph the rule asks the engine for its candidates, then judges each one.

edges.label: candidate, paragraph, list items
edges.summary: Each candidate is tested for placement against its own paragraph and the list items that follow it.

edges.label: known name lookup
edges.summary: A name candidate is placed when it is on the known-names list, word by word or by a known head word.

edges.label: Finding with evidence
edges.summary: Unplaced candidates become findings; name and quoted-term findings carry Statistical evidence.

edges.label: class, group, context, exception, evidence
edges.summary: apply_context resolves each finding, passing the new rule's own evidence and treating older rules as deterministic.

edges.label: Statistical short-circuit
edges.summary: Statistical evidence returns Warning/Advise before class, group, context or exception are consulted.

edges.label: class, group, exception, evidence
edges.summary: RuleMeta::resolve now takes evidence and forwards it to the core resolver.

edges.label: fixture text, context document
edges.summary: The measure suite runs the lint over every fixture and scores the findings against each fixture's target.

edges.label: stop event on stdin
edges.summary: The checkpoint suite spawns the real binary and feeds it a stop event, asserting refusal or non-refusal.

edges.label: label, kind, target, reason
edges.summary: Each fixture's header supplies the ground truth the measure suite scores against.

flows.title: A reply is checked at the stop hook
flows.summary: The stop hook reads the last assistant message, runs the writing lint, and refuses the turn only when a blocking finding survives resolution.

messages.label: read stop event from stdin
messages.note: The event carries the session id and the last assistant message.

response.shape: { kind: Number|Phrase|Time|Name, text: String, range: Range<usize> }

messages.label: Finding with evidence
messages.note: A name or quoted-term finding carries Statistical evidence; a number, phrase or time finding is deterministic.

messages.label: level, remediation
messages.note: Statistical evidence returns Warning/Advise before any other rule is consulted, so a weak-evidence name never refuses the reply.

messages.label: refuse only on a blocking finding
messages.note: A reply whose only finding is a weak-evidence name is let through.

views.title: Architecture overview
views.summary: The stop hook, commit check and scan command feed text into the writing lint, which runs the new unplaceable-reference rule over a candidate engine and a placement test, then resolves each finding through the shared resolver.

children.title: Candidate engine and placement
children.summary: Inside the writing rules: the engine produces candidates per paragraph, the placement test judges each one against the paragraph, and the known-names list is consulted for names.

children.title: Evidence and resolution
children.summary: How a finding's evidence reaches the resolver and short-circuits to an advisory warning.

views.title: Reply stop check
views.summary: The ordered path a reply takes through the stop hook, the new rule, the candidate engine, the placement test and the resolver.
